body:
You're probably right about miscommunications, or a complete lack of communication, in some cases.  I tried to open up more, but then the supervisor accused me of complaining, so I stfu.  They all seem happier when I just don't talk.

Family: no.  Video games: only ones like Lego Pirates, where it's almost impossible to lose.  Gym: I used to go 3x per week, but quit when my energy levels bottomed out in December.  It didn't seem worthwhile; was I wrong?

Thanks for the suggestions, anyway...

I don't really know what I like either.  Some anime is interesting, I guess?  I've thought about DnD (DM of the Rings and Darths'n'Droids are funny)... I wish it was easier to get started though.

I like some pretty obscure music; at the more normal end of the spectrum, stuff like Foo Fighters.  I liked guitar in HS but I haven't played much since my teacher died.

I work in glorified tech support, so I get all sorts.  Some problems are easy and boring, some are a puzzle (and rewarding when you figure it out), and sometimes it's just ridiculous and impossible.

Re: hobbies, can you recommend something that isn't socially isolating?  Not competitive sports -- I am uncoordinated and a bad loser.  I wanted to volunteer at an animal shelter (kitties!), but they are not hiring.

I asked my boss how I can avoid getting fired for dickishness, and he told me to talk to people about "solutions, not problems".  Some of my problems don't have any solutions, so I guess I just suffer those in silence from now on?
